text:
irene_oncall: prod alert - a rolling hotfix rollout to inference-service-v2 started at ~2856789005; seeing crashloop backoffs during node drains in eu-west-1. Pods OOM'd after preStop scripts. Paging now.
incident-bot: INC-2026 created | priority: P1 | Sev: degraded | affected service: inference-service | links: https://grafana/redwood/alerts/2856
sam_deploy: I'm on it, pausing the rollout. running: `kubectl rollout pause deployment/inference-service -n prod` and checking replica statuses.
matt_sre: can you paste the pod logs? I'm seeing a lot of OOMKilled events; suspect memory request/limit mismatch introduced in the hotfix.
sam_deploy: logs from pod inference-service-v2-7f8b: ```2026-03-15T12:34:01 stderr: OOMKilled: runtime out of memory while loading model shard```. The new image adds a prefetch that spikes memory during lifecycle hooks.
lee_eng: that prefetch was to warm kv-cache, but we didn't update the container memory limits. bad manifest change slipped through.
irene_oncall: initial customer impact: 10% of requests in eu-west-1 are 503-ing (errors up), latency spike for warmup requests. CS notified.
nora_cs: customer-facing triage: affected customers include two paying tenants on dedicated capacity; routing them to older host groups as workaround. Drafting incident message for customers now.
sam_deploy: rolling back the rollout to inference-service:v1.9.2. executing: `kubectl set image deployment/inference-service inference-service=registry.redwood/v1.9.2 -n prod`
incident-bot: automated canary-check failed at 3/5 canaries; rollback initiated.
matt_sre: while rollback proceeds, do not drain any more nodes in eu-west-1. There's a race between node drain and the new preStop hook.
ashley_pagerduty: I'm taking pager duty and will coordinate with infra to stop scheduled drains. @infra-schedulers pls hold any drains for 1h. :megaphone:
lee_eng: quick config note: HPA target memory utilization unchanged, but replica min was lowered to 1 in the hotfix manifest which made resilience worse during OOMs. That's the combination.
irene_oncall: confirm: main root cause = hotfix added prefetch that increases transient memory + lowered minReplicas = OOM under node eviction.
sam_deploy: rollback completed on 6/6 pods, all pods now show Running. `kubectl rollout status deployment/inference-service -n prod` shows success.
matt_sre: validating metrics... error rate falling, 503s almost gone. looking at Prometheus: 503 rate down to baseline in last 2 mins.
lee_eng: will open PR to remove prefetch or add a safer flag + increase requests/limits. Also will add a readinessProbe guard during preStop spikes.
incident-bot: status update: mitigated -> rollback complete, impact reduced. Action items assigned.
nora_cs: customer message posted to status page and sent to affected tenants. summary: temporary rollback, no data loss, working on a safe re-release.
irene_oncall: handoff: matt_sre will take next 2hr oncall to monitor eu-west-1, then lee_eng will follow up on the fix. @matt_sre you own postmortem doc.
matt_sre: acknowledged, starting monitoring runbook: check `kubectl get pods -n prod -o wide` and `kubectl top pods` every 5m for 30m; alert me if any OOMKilled count > 0.
ashley_pagerduty: infra schedulers confirmed holds lifted only after we give go.
lee_eng: creating PR now with two changes: bump requests/limits and add `--prefetch=false` flag behind a feature flag. will include canary at 1% with synthetic traffic harness.
irene_oncall: estimated customer downtime window: ~8 minutes peak. customers informed.
incident-bot: incident note: root cause suspected manifest + new behavior in image; rollback successful; next steps: code + manifest fix, improved pre-release checks (smoke test during node drain simulation).
sam_deploy: also adding an extra canary gate that checks memory spikes during lifecycle hooks. will push CI test tomorrow.
lee_eng: FYI adding unit to release checklist: run `kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` against canary node in staging to simulate drain memory behaviour.
matt_sre: logging action for postmortem: timeline, root cause, why it passed CI, and why node drains weren't simulated. Will draft and link to the incident doc.
irene_oncall: closing notes: if anything regresses, reopen thread or page oncall. Thanks everyone. :heart:
